sources.title: Making the V in VQA Matter: Elevating the Role of Image Understanding in Visual Question Answering (Goyal et al.)
sources.role: VQA-v2 balancing authority: complementary-pair construction + language-prior mitigation (source enrichment of the existing VM-D038 candidate)

claims.text: Free-form open-ended VQA task + dataset (~0.25M images, ~0.76M questions, ~10M answers) demanding finer image understanding and complex reasoning than generic captioning, with automatic evaluation via short/multiple-choice answers.
Task-predecessor role: the benchmark family in which the language-prior shortcut was later exposed — D10 control origin shared with VM-O11.
claims.context: Edition-level analytical synthesis by the Work operator (lineage/selection/boundary/contract judgment, not a literal statement of the cited source); structural home for edition rationale.

claims.text: VQA v2 counters language priors by balancing the dataset with complementary image pairs: every question is associated with a pair of similar images that yield two different answers, approximately doubling image-question pairs; state-of-art VQA models perform significantly worse on the balanced set, indicating prior exploitation. The mitigation reduces exploitable question/answer priors and requires greater use of image evidence; it does not eliminate language priors completely.
claims.context: arXiv:1612.00837v3 Abstract + §§1/3/4 (already-bound + newly bound primary sources).

limitations.text: VQA-family accuracy can exploit question/answer priors; VQA v2 reduces this bias using complementary image pairs, so dataset version/split and answer extraction must remain bound to evaluation claims.

targets.finding: Full body consumed: task definition, dataset scale, evaluation design verified.
